root_cause.text: In arm64 contpte, contpte_ptep_set_access_flags() used the gathered ptep_get() view of a contiguous PTE block to detect no-ops, so AF/dirty bits ORed from sibling sub-PTEs could falsely make an individual target sub-PTE appear already updated even though its own access/write bits still required modification.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and patch state that “ptep_get() ORs AF/dirty from all sub-PTEs in the CONT block,” causing “false no-ops when only a sibling has been updated,” and the fix replaces `orig_pte = pte_mknoncont(ptep_get(ptep)); if (pte_val(orig_pte) == pte_val(entry)) return 0;` with `contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags()` that checks raw `__ptep_get()` values for every sub-PTE against `PTE_RDONLY | PTE_AF | PTE_WRITE | PTE_DIRTY`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper that verifies all contiguous sub-PTEs share the same access flags before applying access-flag updates.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function, contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags(pte_t *ptep, pte_t entry), was added before contpte_ptep_set_access_flags(). It aligns the input PTE pointer to the contiguous-PTE base, defines a comparison mask containing PTE_RDONLY, PTE_AF, PTE_WRITE, and PTE_DIRTY, masks those bits from the input entry, iterates over all CONT_PTES sub-PTEs using __ptep_get(), compares the same masked bits for each sub-PTE against the entry, and returns false on the first mismatch or true if all match.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this enables checking whether every sub-PTE in a contiguous PTE group already has the same access-flag-related state as the target entry, while intentionally ignoring PFN differences. It provides a way to detect inconsistent AF/dirty/write/read-only bits across the group so later access-flag updates can avoid applying changes to mismatched entries or handle them correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix contiguous PTE access-flag updates to check all sub-PTEs individually and avoid false no-ops caused by gathered PTE state.
intent_record.what: The change replaces the early no-op check in contpte_ptep_set_access_flags() from comparing entry against pte_mknoncont(ptep_get(ptep)) to calling contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags(ptep, entry), adds a detailed comment explaining why gathered ptep_get() state is insufficient for this decision, and changes orig_pte initialization to use pte_mknoncont(__ptep_get(ptep)) before the later write-bit unfold logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now verifies that every sub-PTE in a contiguous PTE block already has the requested access and write-permission state before treating the update as a no-op. This prevents missed updates when aggregated ptep_get() state makes one sub-PTE appear up to date because a sibling already has AF, dirty, or write permissions set, ensuring the whole CONT range is updated consistently and that write-bit change handling is based on the actual target PTE.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause in contpte access-flag handling by checking that all sub-PTEs in a contiguous block have consistent access flags before treating an update as a no-op, preventing sibling bits from masking needed per-sub-PTE updates.

The group directly fixes the exact root cause: contpte_ptep_set_access_flags() was using a gathered contiguous-PTE view that could mask needed updates due to sibling AF/dirty bits. Checking each sub-PTE individually prevents those false no-op decisions.

candidates.rationale: This statement obtains a gathered view of the entire contiguous PTE range via ptep_get(), which can OR AF/dirty bits from sibling sub-PTEs into orig_pte. That aggregated state is the root cause of falsely concluding the target sub-PTE already has the requested access flags.

This no-op check directly compares the aggregated orig_pte against the desired entry. Because orig_pte may reflect sibling sub-PTE AF/dirty bits rather than the individual target sub-PTE state, the function can wrongly return without applying required access/write updates.
When reached through the flawed equality check, this statement skips the update entirely, embodying the observable vulnerable behavior of treating a needed access-flag change as a no-op.

vuln_statements.explanation: This equality check is the core vulnerable decision point. It compares the desired entry against orig_pte obtained from a gathered contiguous-PTE view, whose AF/dirty bits may be ORed in from sibling sub-PTEs. That can falsely make the target sub-PTE appear already updated, causing a mistaken no-op.

This statement fetches the gathered contiguous-PTE state via ptep_get(ptep), producing an aggregated view rather than the individual target sub-PTE state. That aggregated value feeds the faulty no-op check and is the root cause source of the incorrect comparison.
When executed after the flawed equality check, this return skips the necessary access-flag update entirely, resulting in the observable vulnerable behavior.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full body of the relevant function `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags()` and also the helper `contpte_ptep_get()` that determines the semantics of `ptep_get(ptep)` for contpte mappings. The vulnerable construct is present in `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags()` at `orig_pte = pte_mknoncont(ptep_get(ptep));` followed immediately by `if (pte_val(orig_pte) == pte_val(entry)) return 0;`. Per the root cause, this no-op detection is wrong because `ptep_get(ptep)` for a contpte mapping does not return the target sub-PTE's own AF/dirty state; instead, `contpte_ptep_get()` explicitly 'Gather[s] access/dirty bits' from the whole contiguous range and ORs them into `orig_pte` via `if (pte_dirty(pte)) orig_pte = pte_mkdirty(orig_pte);` and `if (pte_young(pte)) orig_pte = pte_mkyoung(orig_pte);`. Therefore, sibling sub-PTEs can make `orig_pte` appear already young/dirty even when the specific target PTE still needs updating, causing the equality check to falsely conclude 'noop'. The fix would require avoiding this gathered/block-wide view for the no-op check and using the target PTE's own state instead. That handling is not present here, so the function contains the bug and is not yet fixed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is fully visible in `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause says this function incorrectly uses the gathered `ptep_get()` view of a contiguous PTE block to detect no-ops, allowing AF/dirty bits from sibling sub-PTEs to make the target sub-PTE appear already updated. That exact pattern is present here: `orig_pte = pte_mknoncont(ptep_get(ptep));` followed immediately by `if (pte_val(orig_pte) == pte_val(entry)) return 0;`. In this file, `contpte_ptep_get()` explicitly gathers young/dirty bits from all PTEs in the contiguous range: `if (pte_dirty(pte)) orig_pte = pte_mkdirty(orig_pte);` and `if (pte_young(pte)) orig_pte = pte_mkyoung(orig_pte);`. Using that aggregated value for the no-op test can falsely conclude no change is needed even when the target PTE itself still lacks the needed access/write-related state. There is no visible fix here to avoid using the aggregated `ptep_get()` result for the no-op comparison; instead, the buggy comparison is present as introduced.
